subject: Private deployment crosswalk: aligning Terraform, Helm, and Ansible in CI
messages:
From: InfraOps Solutions <eng@infraops.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: platform@acmebio.com
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: crosswalk for ACME private deployment (Terraform/Helm/Ansible)

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the intro call this morning. ACME's infra team asked us to lay out a concrete crosswalk between the Terraform modules that provision the VPC/subnets and the Helm charts/values and Ansible roles that configure the host-level runtime (bastion, monitoring agents, certs). They asked for a CI validation matrix that ensures a pull request touching any of the three areas (tf/helm/ansible) runs the appropriate integration checks and smoke deploy to a sandbox.

We drafted an initial spreadsheet attached that maps resources (VPC, subnets, route tables, NAT, TLSPolicy) to chart values and ansible roles. We also included a proposed gating flow: 1) terraform plan & unit tests, 2) helm lint + render + values consistency check, 3) ansible syntax + idempotency run on a local VM image, 4) combined dry-run in sandbox.

High-level ask: can your IaC team review the attached crosswalk and confirm what automation we should add to Redwood's CI to ensure safe rollouts for private deployments? In particular, ACME needs evidence that artifact signing, image provenance, and network ACL changes are validated before merge.

Attachments: iac-crosswalk.xlsx (spreadsheet), vpc-network-diagram.pdf (diagram)

--
Tomas Reyes
InfraOps Solutions
eng@infraops.com

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: InfraOps Solutions <eng@infraops.com>, platform@acmebio.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: crosswalk for ACME private deployment (Terraform/Helm/Ansible)

Tomas — thanks, received and skimmed. Folks, looping you in; I attached a lightweight deployment-matrix.md that captures the verification steps we can wire into GitLab CI and the gate conditions for Dedicated/Private rollouts.

Quick notes after a first pass:
- Good mapping overall. We should be explicit about the source-of-truth for each resource: terraform state for infra, values.yaml for chart-level config, and inventory/hostvars for ansible.
- Artifact signing: agree this must be enforced for images and terraform modules. We use cosign for container images; for terraform modules there is a signing pipeline (module-provenance) that can attach provenance metadata.
- Sandbox validation: propose a two-stage sandbox: "render-only" (helm template + tf plan compare) and "ephemeral-sandbox" (full apply to ephemeral VPC + bootstrap ansible). The sandbox apply should be constrained and timeboxed.

Next steps: karthik — can you review the matrix and call out any blocking module changes (naming, outputs, exported IDs)? Neha — please list any compliance evidence items ACME will require (logs, audit trail, signed artifacts). Vanessa — can you confirm owner for the CI job templates and whether we should add a new job flavor (priv-sandbox-validate) to our shared templates repo.

I've attached the markdown and the quick ansible role inventory (ansible-role-list.txt).

Attachments: deployment-matrix.md, ansible-role-list.txt

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Platform PM, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, InfraOps Solutions <eng@infraops.com>, platform@acmebio.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment crosswalk: aligning Terraform, Helm, and Ansible in CI

Thanks Hannah — reviewed the sheet and the matrix. A few technical clarifications and one recommended change:

1) Terraform outputs vs. Helm values: several modules currently expose the private subnet IDs as "private_subnet_ids" list. Many of our Helm charts expect a single comma-delimited string for the kube-proxy allowed CIDRs. We should standardize on structured output (list) and add a small rendering helper in the shared infra-lib (go/python) that converts lists -> expected helm value formats. That avoids inline hacks in every chart's pipeline.

2) Module boundaries: the ingress/egress NAT module needs to export the nat-gateway-ids and public-eip mappings. ACME's security team will require mapping between NATs and source CIDRs for audit. Please add these outputs to the module (backwards compatible as optional outputs).

3) CI gating: for any PR that updates terraform state-affecting files we should run: terraform fmt/check, terraform plan (against a mocked state in the CI workspace), and a policy check (conftest/OPA) with our priv-deploy rules. For helm changes, add a values-consistency job that invokes the rendering helper and fails if values diverge. For ansible, run molecule with the idempotency scenario but inside a lightweight container image (no privileged network changes).

4) Sandbox teardown: we must ensure the ephemeral sandbox auto-destroys on pipeline failure or completion (TTL policy). Add a final job step that records the sandbox id and the artifact list to the provenance store.

I added inline comments in the GitHub PR (see link) and pushed a small utility "tf->helm-render" in my feature branch.

-Karthik
Lead Infra Engineer

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: InfraOps Solutions <eng@infraops.com>, platform@acmebio.com
Date: Fri, 06 Aug 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment crosswalk: aligning Terraform, Helm, and Ansible in CI

All — good thread. Quick decisions and action items so we can move this to implementation:

Decisions:
- Add "priv-sandbox-validate" job to shared-ci-templates (must include ttl, artifact-signing step, and provenance upload).
- Require cosign-signed container images and signed terraform module bundles for any private-deploy merge.
- Add "render helper" to infra-lib and ship as version 0.1 in the shared artifacts registry.

Action items (owners):
- karthik_iyer: finalize tf outputs (nat-gateway mappings, private_subnet_ids normalization) + PR to modules repo by 2026-08-13.
- neha_kapoor: compile ACME evidence checklist (audit logs, KMS keys used, retention policy) and share with ACME by 2026-08-10.
- hannah_schmitt: draft CI template (priv-sandbox-validate) and create follow-up PR with examples by 2026-08-12.
- vanessa_ortiz: own merging policy and ensure release checklist includes provenance tagging.

Links: github PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/privdeploy/pull/412 (karthik's render helper), drive folder https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-iac-crosswalk (working docs), JIRA PRIV-2337 (track epic).

I'll create the shared-CI issue and add the template tasks. If ACME wants a synchronous review we'll schedule a 30-min working session next week.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
